question: When a fake video of a real person spreads online, who should be responsible for stopping the harm?
reflection: Clear labels and fair rules for fake media can protect people's dignity and keep public debate honest for everyone.

one_line: Pressure grows on platforms and labs to prove their AI is safe, while AI tools for specific professions such as law arrive.

top_stories.title: Meta told its deepfake safeguards fall short
top_stories.what: Meta's Oversight Board ordered the removal of AI-made videos that falsely showed two real people in the UK, and called the company's deepfake protections inadequate.
top_stories.why: Clear rules for labelling and demoting fake media are a public-trust issue that behavioural research can test before they are rolled out.

top_stories.title: A legal edition of a frontier model
top_stories.what: OpenAI launched a version of GPT-6 Astra for law firms, linked to a daily-updated index of US case law and rules, with access for approved firms first.
top_stories.why: Profession-specific models show where general chatbots fall short, and the same path could follow for policy or social research.

top_stories.title: Amazon and others push for testing before release
top_stories.what: Amazon said models should launch only after rigorous safety testing, and a new partnership with Hugging Face plans open safety tools for open-weight models.
top_stories.why: Growing demand for evidence of safety opens a role for independent evaluation, including tests of how real users behave with a model.

saudi_lens.text: Huawei is bringing forward its next AI chip, which may widen the choice of hardware suppliers that Gulf data-centre projects can consider, within the limits of export rules.

idea.title: Deepfake label test
idea.pitch: Test which warning labels on AI-made videos actually change whether Arabic-speaking viewers believe and share them.
idea.fit: Government digital services, media regulator, culture sector
idea.first_step: Prepare three label wordings and one harmless sample clip for a small online experiment.

idea_kids.title: The machine that only pretends to listen
idea_kids.pitch: A short picture book about a child who talks to a simple chatbot and slowly learns it matches words without truly understanding.
idea_kids.first_step: Write a ten-page story outline with one simple rule the chatbot follows on each page.

terms.definition: A fake video, image or audio clip made with AI to look or sound like a real person.
A technique that strips the built-in safety refusals out of an open-weight model.

concepts.summary: Platforms face pressure to label, demote and remove AI-made fakes of real people.
Calls grow for proof of safety testing before models are released.
Top labs tune their general models for single professions such as law.
